Pickup 30 min after clearance; English-speaking guide + name placard at arrival hall
Officially **'Civilian-Military Complex Port for Beautiful Tourism'** — opened Feb 2016
**53-bus outdoor parking** — fills fast on dual-ship days; guides arrive early
Better **wheelchair accessibility** than Jeju Port (north) — flat interior, elevators
**Adora Magic City semi-homeport since May 1, 2025** — 33 roundtrips planned
Southern itinerary is mandatory from this port — Seongsan is 70+ min one-way

/itinerary_variants/1/stops/0/whyOnRoute.source_en: **Gangjeong is the only viable origin for the south route** — its dual-berth 220,000-ton capacity makes it the cruise gateway for larger ships (Adora Magic City, MSC, Costa, etc.) that exceed Jeju Port's 140,000 GT limit. All four southern POIs (Hallasan 1100 / Jusangjeolli / Cheonjiyeon / Olle Market) sit within a **30-min radius of this port**, building a comfortable 8-hour day with zero long transit blocks. For a **bus tour**, the 53-bus parking capacity is the key schedule limit on dual-ship days — the operator's standard practice is to arrive 15 minutes early to secure a coach slot, ensuring guests don't wait at curbside after disembarkation.

/itinerary_variants/1/stops/0/descriptio.source_en: Your driver and English-speaking guide meet your party at the **Gangjeong Port Cruise Terminal** in Seogwipo, the main cruise terminal on Jeju's southern coast. Pickup is timed around your ship's clearance and the guide carries a name sign or clear meeting information. Because Gangjeong is close to Seogwipo, the south route can cover Hallasan 1100 Highland, Jusangjeolli Cliff, ⟦G0⟧, and ⟦G1⟧ without the long cross-island drive required from Jeju Port. Before departure, the guide confirms the all-aboard time, weather, walking pace, and any ship-specific return requirements.

/itinerary_variants/1/stops/1/whyOnRoute.source_en: **Hallasan 1100 Highland gives the south route a cool mountain opening.** The wetland area sits high on the road across Hallasan and offers an easy boardwalk-style nature stop without a major hike. It works well for cruise guests because the visit is scenic, relatively simple to manage with a group, and naturally placed between Gangjeong Port and the south-coast stops.

/itinerary_variants/1/stops/1/descriptio.source_en: **⟦G0⟧ (한라산 1100고지 습지)** is a high-elevation alpine wetland system on the Hallasan plateau, located **at exactly 1,100 m above sea level** along **Route 1100 — the highest national highway in Korea** linking Jeju City to Seogwipo Jungmun. The site is a **Ramsar Wetland of International Importance (Site No. 1893, designated 12 October 2009)**, falling within the **Hallasan UNESCO World Heritage Site (2007)**, **Jeju Island UNESCO Biosphere Reserve (2002)**, and **Hallasan National Park (1970)** — making this one of the few sites globally with **four overlapping international/national designations**. The wetland comprises **16+ discontinuous freshwater marshes and pools** spread across a low-gradient plateau section that captures and retains rainwater, forming **small permanent lakes and peat bogs** that support diverse floristic assemblages with significant Jeju endemism. Recorded biodiversity includes **3 threatened bird species and 1 threatened plant species within Korea**, plus mammal, reptile, and insect species endemic to Jeju Island. The site received **900,000 visitors in 2008** (Mt Halla Visitor Centre data). Visitor experience: a **1-km wooden boardwalk loop** with observation decks, interpretive signage, and a small natural-history exhibit at the trailhead. **Autumn foliage (October–November)** and **winter snow scenes (December–February)** are the most photographed seasons; **spring + summer** offer wetland flora and endemic species visibility. **FREE admission**; adjacent **1100 Rest Area (1100 휴게소)** provides indoor restrooms + cafe + small souvenir shop. **Cultural and religious importance** to local communities is documented in the Ramsar listing — historical shaman pilgrimages tied to mountain-water spirits.

/itinerary_variants/1/stops/2/highlights.source_en: **Natural Monument No. 443** — designated **2005-01-06**, the most recent Jeju coastal NM
Columns rise **30–40 m**, packed in **5- to 7-sided polygons** (mostly hexagons) along **1 km** of coastline
Formation: **Hallasan flank lava cooled in the sea ~250,000–140,000 years ago**, contracting perpendicular to cooling face
**East Asia's premier columnar-jointing site** — peer to Giant's Causeway, Devils Postpile, Fingal's Cave
